reason: A's Day 3 is physically impossible: it walks the Kalalau Trail at Ke'e, then drives '20 min / 6 km' to Kalalau Lookout, which is at Koke'e on the other side of Na Pali. It also gives no Ha'ena reservation, and from a Poipu base it makes three north-shore runs (Days 2, 3, 6) for a garden and Lumahai. B's Princeville base gets Hanalei Bay and Kilauea Point right (Day 2), but it understates the two west-side days (Days 6–7) at about 2.5 h each way, and Day 1 'stargazing' at 18:00 is before the 18:46 sunset. Neither plan has a Na Pali boat or hurricane-season note; B is merely less broken.

Both keep one Baixa/Chiado base on foot and transit, and both miss Jeronimos. A reaches Belem only for pasteis (Day 3), zig-zags by train between Feira da Ladra, Time Out, Belem and the castle, and puts an unrequested 05:30 breakfast and sunrise square on departure day. B is geographically tighter and includes fado and the castle, but it labels Senhora do Monte 'at sunset' at 16:30 (sunset is 20:40) and skips Belem. That is a narrow edge to B.

Tenerife from a single Puerto de la Cruz base fits a mild late-March family retreat: easy coast walks, Anaga, La Orotava, a beach day and long free afternoons. It has faults: Day 4 places Santa Cruz a '10 min walk' from Puerto de la Cruz, Teide by day is missing, and arrival night runs stargazing to midnight. B's Turangi base has real thermal pools (Tokaanu), but Day 5 starts at 05:30 with the strenuous 7 h Tongariro Alpine Crossing, then stacks a market, trout centre and kayak until 19:00. Day 9 adds a 5 h Tama Lakes hike, and typical driving runs about 145 min a day, which goes against 'feel good' with children. B's shortlist also offers Bali in its wet season.

Both use the same four bases, both drive past Jokulsarlon without stopping (a hard failure), and both skip Myvatn and Godafoss. A at least has Dettifoss (Day 5), Seljalandsfoss and a Golden Circle soak (Secret Lagoon, Day 8). B has Husavik whale watching and Hoffell pools, but labels Dyrholaey 'at sunset' at 16:30 when sunset is near midnight, spends Day 8 on Laugavegur shopping and Harpa, and names a Vik restaurant for dinner in Hofn. Both visit Dyrholaey during the nesting closure.

Both wrongly make a self-drive car and one base the frame, with no inn-to-inn walking or luggage shuttle. A's Hongu base is central: it walks four Kodo sections (Days 2, 3, 4, 6), includes Yunomine onsen and all three Grand Shrines plus the river boat, and its main flaw is a 05:30 departure-day viewpoint. B's Nachisan base adds about 135 min of driving a day. It walks only two short sections, and Day 5 is roadside oji stops by car; its one-way-walk transport notes are a useful touch.

Neither plan has Song-Kul, a yurt night or a multi-day trek, which are the core of the request. A at least moves to Karakol after an Ala Archa acclimatisation day and does a strenuous Altyn Arashan day (Day 10), though the 7 h 50 bus is realistic and the Saturday 'Sunday animal market' with a 05:30 start is wrong. B never leaves Bishkek in 10 nights: museums, a philharmonic evening, empty afternoons and Papa John's, with Kol-Tor as its only real hike. B itself admits it lacks the destination's defining experiences.

Both miss the Tre Cime circuit and Seceda. A's Cortina base gives Sorapis and an early Braies visit, but it drives about 2 h each way to Catinaccio (starting 11:05) and to Alpe di Siusi, and schedules a Lagazuoi sunset dinner until 22:20 with no way down. Day 2 also adds an after-dinner drive to Santa Croce. B's Corvara base keeps driving to about 95 min and has more genuine hikes: Cinque Torri plus Ra Gusela, Scotoni to Lagazuoi, and the Sass de Putia circuit. Its faults are an unrequested 05:30 Val di Funes start, 'stargazing' at 18:00 in July and a via ferrata named with no gear guidance.

A breaks two hard rules for a grandparent trip: two bases (Lagos, then Tavira on Day 5) and a 05:30 start on Day 4. It also has invented train legs, such as a train to Ponta da Piedade. A does have more beach time (Dona Ana, Ilha Deserta, Ilha de Tavira). B keeps one Lagos base and no early starts, with Luz beach, a dolphin boat, Silves and cool Monchique. Its weaknesses are fictional trains, a Vilamoura day at 1 h 45 each way, and Camilo's stairs, which are hard on grandparents.

A is a real northern-circuit safari: Arusha, Tarangire, two Karatu nights with an early crater descent, three Serengeti nights and a flight back, all by guided 4x4. Its flaws are a Mara day trip from central Serengeti costed at '2 hr', a crossing implied as the highlight on 11 July, and a stray rental-car booking line. B places 'Serengeti game drives' a 15-minute walk from central Arusha (Day 4), so there is effectively no Serengeti and no Tarangire. It also routes everything by non-existent trains.

A never goes to Kyoto: it is 7 Tokyo nights plus 2 in Hakone, it is planned around a rental car against the stated by-train request, and Hakone Day 9 starts at 05:30. B does Tokyo 4 and Kyoto 5 by train with the core Kyoto sights: Nijo, Nishiki, Gion, Kiyomizu, Ginkaku-ji, Kinkaku-ji, Arashiyama and Fushimi Inari. Its Day 5 is broken, though: it sends the couple back to Meiji Jingu in Tokyo after arriving in Kyoto, with three 3.5 h trains. Neither addresses the late Tokyo blossom.
